newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen opening mixed to slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen opening mixed to slightly lower.

text.p: Wall Street is expected to open mixed to a bit lower Monday amid profit-taking following last week's strong rise, analysts said.
With no economic data due today, investors are expected to focus on corporate earnings.
Before the market opened, Dow industrials component AT&T Corp reported first quarter operating earnings of $0.69 a share, in line with the First Call consensus estimate.
"After last week's spectacular rise, the market here is probably headed for some profit-taking," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
The Dow rose 44.95 points Friday to close at 6.703.55 and was up 311.86 points on the week, the biggest one-week gain in the index's history.
Cardillo said U.S. stocks could head higher if yields on the U.S. Treasury 30-year bond hit seven percent, "and that's only 50-50." The bond was trading down 1/32 to yield 7.06 percent.
Thom Brown, managing director at Rutherford Brown and Catherwood, said markets were focusing on the prospect of the Fed raising interest rates next month.
This week's major economic data are due Friday, when the government reports March existing home sales. The forecast is for sales at an annual rate of 4.14 million, down from 4.26 million in February.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average rose sharply to finish up 199.52 points, or 1.09 percent, at 18,551.66.
In London the FTSE 100 index was down 1.8 points at 4308.7.
U.S. shares were mostly firmer in London in light volume as investors fretted about the sustainability of the Dow's recent rally.
The dollar fell sharply against the mark in Tokyo as traders sold dollars for marks to cut losses on their long positions. The dollar firmed against the mark in Europe.
The Wall Street Journal's "Heard on the Street" column said possible new curbs on cigarette advertising may put pressure on ad firms that get the business.
